title: Black ops Zombie Mode | Kimi K3 + Cline/Openrouter | ~9$ Cost
author: RecordingTechnical86
selftext:
Hey guys,

I wanted to test Kimi K3 and used the Openrouter API with Cline in VS Code.

Prompt: Create bo2 zombie mode as good as possible in three.js. Fun and juice is the most important aspect.

Had to fix 2 bugs: Lag on head explode + cant open doors, thats it

It came out pretty fun and good looking, especially for an open source model. Using a gateway that supports Prompt caching would have saved some cost. Its definetely possible to get this done cheaper.

comments.author: robotpoolparty
comments.body: Port this to a VR game, while thinking of ways to have player be more stationary to avoid VR motion sickness, and you might have a popular game in that market.

replies.body: Pavlov VR with the Black ops Kino der Toten Map is already unbeatable ;)

replies.author: RecordingTechnical86
replies.body: It is! That's what i meant. Kimi K3 seems to have more understanding of what makes a game fun for the player not only on paper

replies.author: RecordingTechnical86
replies.body: Thank you, one could make a splitscreen version

comments.author: FutureLynx_
comments.body: Is Kimi K3 as good as Claude as they are saying? Isnt it supposed to be a free alternative? Why the 9$?

replies.author: RecordingTechnical86
replies.body: It is pretty good as you can see. Its not free to autonomously code. You can get it for 5$ on opencode atm. For this experiment i used Cline which is an autocoder that does not support prompt caching with Kimi K3. Thats why it cost so much. Realistically you could get this done with under 5$ using the opencode subscription
